subject: DPA negotiation: residency, snapshot retention, and onshore-wipe options
messages:
From: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@acmehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Health Legal <legal@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on residency, backups, and deletion windows

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for sending the draft DPA. Our legal team has a few focused questions so we can circulate an initial redline:

1) Residency: we need confirmation of where logs, backups, and generated output are stored for EU customers. Is primary data processed in EU regions exclusively when EU residency is selected?

2) Backups: what is the retention for system backups and disaster-recovery copies? Are backups excluded from customer deletion requests or are they subject to the same erase window?

3) Deletion/erase window: your draft lists 30 days for deletion of primary stores — does that include snapshots and backups? Can you provide proposed onshore-wipe language for when the contract terminates or we request data erasure?

4) Legal hold: we need a mechanism to pause deletion for litigation/regulatory holds and a notice process; can that be added?

Would appreciate short answers or a redline we can review. If easier, happy to schedule a 30-minute call next week.

Best,
Sophie Martin
Senior Privacy Counsel
Acme Health

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-02T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Questions on residency, backups, and deletion windows

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Rachel (Legal) and Priyom (Security/Compliance) to propose precise language.

Quick answers to keep things moving:
- Residency: when a customer elects EU residency, Redwood processes and stores primary Customer Data and generated outputs in our EU regions. Access controls and encryption keys for EU-resident customers are managed in-region by default.
- Backups: our operational snapshots are retained for business continuity; standard snapshot retention is 90 days. Backups that contain Customer Data are subject to deletion processes but may have a different timeline than primary stores.
- Deletion window: 30 days applies to primary production stores. For backups and snapshots we can commit contractually to a bounded purge window (commonly 90 days) with exceptions for lawful retention or legal hold.
- Legal hold: Redwood supports a written legal-hold process that suspends automated deletion; we keep an auditable record of holds.

Rachel/Priyom — can you draft two redline options (conservative and balanced) and I'll attach them to our reply? Sophie — we can also do a short call Wed/Thu next week to walk the redline.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-10-05T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Questions on residency, backups, and deletion windows

Jordan / Priyom — per request, drafted two concise redline snippets and answered Sophie's questions inline below. I'll attach the full redline if useful.

Sophie — answers and proposed contract text:

1) Residency (proposed):
"When Customer elects EU residency, Redwood will process and store Customer Data and derivative outputs within Redwood's European processing locations and will not transfer Customer Data outside the European Economic Area except with Customer's prior written consent or where necessary for availability with documented safeguards."

Operational note: primary data and outputs remain in EU; logs are kept in-region where feasible. Cross-region replication for DR is disabled by default for EU-resident customers unless expressly enabled.

2) Backups (conservative redline):
"Redwood may retain backups and disaster recovery copies of Customer Data for up to ninety (90) days after such data is deleted from primary systems. Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to purge Customer Data from backups within ninety (90) days of Customer's deletion request or contract termination, except to the extent retention is required by applicable law or by a documented legal hold."

Operational note: backups are encrypted with customer-scoped keys; for EU residency customers, KMS keys are region-controlled by default.

3) Deletion / Onshore wipe (balanced redline):
"Upon Customer's written deletion request or upon contract termination, Redwood will delete Customer Data from primary production systems within thirty (30) days. Redwood will take commercially reasonable efforts to remove Customer Data from backups and DR copies within ninety (90) days. For customers requiring onshore-only wipe commitments, Redwood will agree an addendum describing an onshore-wipe plan, timeline, and any additional fees for the operational effort."

4) Legal hold (redline):
"If Customer provides a written legal hold notice, Redwood will suspend automatic deletion for the specified Customer Data and preserve the data for the duration of the hold. Redwood will maintain an audit log of all legal hold requests and release notices and will notify Customer when automated deletion resumes."

Next steps: Jordan — I can produce the redline document (attached) with these options and a brief cover note. Sophie — happy to do a 30-minute call to confirm positions.

Regards,
Rachel Kim
Head of Legal | Redwood Inference
